record.title: MAGI: Multi-Agent Guided Interview for Psychiatric Assessment
record.reason: Dedicated psychiatric assessment via MINI-based multi-agent interviewing and DSM-5-aligned PsyCoT. Main experiments address depression, generalized/social anxiety and suicide-risk expert agreement, not incidental medical prompts. Authors describe1002 university mental-health interview sessions with two licensed expert annotators; dialogue-quality comparisons additionally use LLM-simulated participants, which must remain distinct. Page9 reports informed consent and non-diagnostic research boundaries, no AI analyses directly shared with participants, and clinical diagnoses reserved for psychiatrists. No treatment efficacy or deployment safety is established here. Formal Long/Short remains pending; complete profile independently assigned.

record.scope_reason: GFD fuses general text-recognition and language models. Physical pages 5 and 7 evaluate multilingual ASR/OCR, long-form lectures, rare-word recognition and instructions. Medical symptom-tag transcription is a genuine domain-conditioned sub-experiment alongside LibriSpeech, FormosaSpeech and air-traffic control, not a biomedical-primary study.

record.title: HPSS: Heuristic Prompting Strategy Search for LLM Evaluators
record.scope_reason: HPSS optimizes generic LLM evaluators. Physical pages 6–7 evaluate summarization Summeval, dialogue Topical-Chat, hotel/restaurant data-to-text SFHOT/SFRES, story HANNA and general pairwise benchmarks. No biomedical-primary task.

record.title: A Fully Generative Motivational Interviewing Counsellor Chatbot for Moving Smokers Towards the Decision to Quit
record.scope_reason: Medical-primary smoking cessation counselling: physical pages 5–7 and 9–10 describe GPT-4o MIBot and AutoMISC in a feasibility study of 106 adult smokers recruited through Prolific. Self-reported confidence increased 1.7/10 at one week; readiness change was not significant. This was not a randomized controlled trial and historical human-counsellor comparisons are not matched experimental controls. The authors explicitly do not claim fully effective therapy.

record.scope_reason: The article improves concise chain-of-thought reasoning on GSM8K and MATH mathematical tasks. The complete abstracts do not describe a biomedical-primary problem.

record.title: Reason from Future: Reverse Thought Chain Enhances LLM Reasoning
record.scope_reason: RFF is general bidirectional reasoning. Physical pages 6–8 evaluate Game of 24, GSM8K, SVAMP, ASDiv, MATH-500, CommonQA and LogiQA. These are mathematical and commonsense reasoning, not medical reasoning benchmarks.

record.title: LLMs as Planning Formalizers: A Survey for Leveraging Large Language Models to Construct Automated Planning Models
record.scope_reason: The survey concerns LLMs as formalizers for classical planning. Its complete abstracts describe general planning architectures/formalization rather than a medical-primary planning review.

record.title: From Conversation to Automation: Leveraging LLMs for Problem-Solving Therapy Analysis
record.scope_reason: Medical-primary analysis of Problem-Solving Therapy: physical pages 3–5 and 8–9 use 240 PISCES sessions involving 152 hospice family caregivers, with 500 manually annotated utterances and 5000 GPT-labelled training examples. GPT-4o annotates PST strategies and therapeutic dynamics; ModernBERT is distilled from pseudo-labels. The abstracts call .76 accuracy, whereas Table1 and conclusion identify weighted F1 .76. This is therapy-session annotation and discourse analysis, not validated treatment efficacy; English transcripts omit tone and nonverbal cues.

record.title: Revisiting Self-Consistency from Dynamic Distributional Alignment Perspective on Answer Aggregation
record.scope_reason: Dynamic-temperature self-consistency targets mathematical reasoning. The full abstracts identify reasoning efficiency and answer aggregation rather than biomedical tasks.

record.title: Don’t Say No: Jailbreaking LLM by Suppressing Refusal
record.scope_reason: DSN studies general adversarial suffixes and refusal suppression. Physical page 5 evaluates AdvBench, JailbreakBench, Malicious Instruct, CLAS and Forbidden Question using HarmBench/refusal metrics. It is general model safety evaluation, not a biomedical-primary task.

record.title: DiaLLMs: EHR-Enhanced Clinical Conversational System for Clinical Test Recommendation and Diagnosis Prediction
record.reason: DiaLLM is a dedicated EHR-grounded clinical dialogue/test-recommendation/diagnosis system. Actual experiments use NHANES diabetes8897patients and TriNetX33105de-identified patients for metabolic, respiratory and circulatory disease prediction. EHR-to-dialogue conversion and clinical-test reference/interpretation are central, with retrospective single/multi-turn prediction and expert input. Page9 explicitly says real-world clinical reliability is not established and requires clinician oversight/validation. Formal Long/Short pending; no treatment-effect inference.

record.title: Enhancing Medical Dialogue Generation through Knowledge Refinement and Dynamic Prompt Adjustment
record.reason: MedRef specifically generates medical doctor responses through medical-knowledge refinement and dynamically selected triplets/demonstrations. Main MedDG/KaMed experiments measure response similarity, medical-entity F1 and human fluency/knowledge/quality ratings. This is dedicated healthcare dialogue research, while benchmark scores and illustrative cases do not establish patient benefit or real-world reliability. Authors position it as assistive and require qualified-provider consultation. Formal Long/Short pending.
